questions.q: What does the built-in readWrite role grant?
options: Read and write access to a database's data, without administrative privileges
Only the ability to manage users, not touch data
Full superuser access to the entire deployment
Only the ability to create and drop indexes
questions.explain: readWrite grants read and write access to a database's data but stops short of admin tasks like user management.

questions.q: What does the dbOwner role combine?
options: read access across every database on the deployment
Only userAdmin, with no data access at all
readWrite, dbAdmin, and userAdmin on a single database — effectively full control of that database
root access across the entire cluster
questions.explain: dbOwner bundles readWrite, dbAdmin, and userAdmin into full control scoped to one database.

questions.q: What does db.createRole() let you do that built-in roles can't?
options: Bypass authentication entirely for that role
Create a new database automatically
Assign a role without ever needing db.grantRolesToUser()
Grant an exactly-scoped set of actions on an exact resource, like only find on one specific collection
questions.explain: Custom roles let you define privileges down to specific actions on specific resources, narrower than any built-in role.

questions.q: Can a single MongoDB user hold multiple roles scoped to different databases?
options: Only the root role can span multiple databases
Only if all the roles are custom roles
No, a user can only ever have one role total
Yes — db.grantRolesToUser() accepts an array of {role, db} pairs
questions.explain: grantRolesToUser takes an array, so a user can hold different roles scoped to different databases simultaneously.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the recommended practice for an application's database connection user?
options: Give every application user the dbOwner role on every database
Always use the root role so the application never hits a permissions error
Grant exactly the roles its workload needs, typically scoped readWrite on its own database — not root or dbOwner
Applications should never authenticate at all
questions.explain: The lesson reinforces least privilege: broad roles like root or dbOwner should be reserved for actual administrators, not embedded in application connections.
